a dispersion: δ. τῶν Ἑλλήνων, Jo 7:35; metaph., of Christians (DB, iii, 782 f.), Ja 1:1, I Pe 1:1 (v. Hort, in ll.).†

Δίδυμος.long: the Twin; Didymus, the Greek name equivalent to Thomas.
Δίδυμος.sd: double, i.e. twin; Didymus, a Christian
Δίδυμος.as:
Δίδυμος, -ου, ὁ
(prop. name from δίδυμος, -η, -ον, double, sc. παῖς, twin)
Didymus, surname of the apostle Thomas: Jo 11:1620:2421:2.†

δεκαπέντε.as:
† δεκα-πέντε
[in LXX: Ex 27:15, I Mac 10:40, al. ;]
late form of πεντεκαίδεκα, fifteen: Jo 11:18, Ac 27:5, WH, mg., ib. 28, Ga 1:18.†

δακρύω.as:
δακρύω
[in LXX for בָּכָה, etc. ;]
to weep, shed tears: Jo 11:35.†
SYN.: κλαίω, of audible weeping, to cry; ὀδύρομαι, of grief expressed verbally, to lament; θρηνέω, of formal lamentation, to sing a dirge; ἀλαλάζω, to wail in Oriental fashion; στενάζω, of grief expressed by inarticulate sounds, to groan.

διαζώννυμι.long: I gird, tie around; mid: I gird round myself.
διαζώννυμι.as:
δια-ζώννυμι, (also -ννύω)
[in LXX for חֲגוֹר, Ez 23:15 A * ;]
to gird round: ἑαυτόν, Jo 13:4; pass., ib. 13:5; mid., to gird oneself with: c. acc, Jo 21:7.†

δειλιάω.long: I shrink, am fearful, timid, cowardly.
δειλιάω.as:
† δειλιάω, -ῶ
(< δειλία), [in LXX for חתת ni., פּחד, etc. ;]
= the more freq. ἀποδ-, to be cowardly, timid, fearful: Jo 14:27.†

διάλεκτος.long: language, speech, conversation, manner of speaking.
διάλεκτος.as:
διά-λεκτος, -ου, ἡ
(< διαλέγομαι), [in LXX: Da LXX 1:4 (לָשׁוֹן), Es 9:26 * ;]
1.conversation, discourse, speech (Plat., Dem., al.).
2. As in Polyb. and later writers, the language or dialect of a particular country or district: Ac 1:192:6, 821:4022:226:14.†

διαχλευάζω.as:
* δια-χλευάζω, intensive of χλευάζω,
to scoff, mock:
(a) c. acc;
(b) absol., Ac 2:13.†

διαφθορά.as:
δια-φθορά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(< διαφθείρω), [in LXX chiefly for שׁחת, and cogn. forms ;]
1.destruction.
2.corruption (physical or moral): of the grave, Ac 2:27(LXX), Ac 2:3113:34-37.†

διαπονέομαι.sd: to toil through, i.e. (passively) be worried
διαπονέομαι.der: from G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G4192 (πόνος);
διαπονέομαι.as:
δια-πονέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Ec 10:9 (עצב ni.), II Mac 2:28; in Aq.: Ge 6:6, I Ki 20:3 * ;]
to work out with labour. Pass., to be worn out, sore troubled: Mk 14:4 (WH, mg.), Ac 4:216:18.†

διανέμω.long: I divide into portions, distribute; pass: I am spread about.
διανέμω.sd: to distribute, i.e. (of information) to disseminate
διανέμω.der: from G1223 (διά) and the base of G3551 (νόμος);
διανέμω.as:
δια-νέμω
[in LXX for חלק, De 29:26(25) * ;]
to distribute, divide: pass., to be spread about, Ac 4:17.†

διάστημα.as:
διάστημα, -τος, τό
(< διίστημι), [in LXX for רֶוַח, etc.;]
an interval, space: of time (Si, prol.24), Ac 5:7.†

δημόσιος.sd: public; (feminine singular dative case as adverb) in public
δημόσιος.as:
** δημόσιος, -α, -ον
(< δῆμος), [in LXX: II Mac 6:10, III Mac 2:274:7 * ;]
belonging to the people, public: Ac 5:18; dat. fem. used adverbially (cl.);
(a)at the public expense, by public consent;
(b)publicly: Ac 16:3718:2820:20.†

διαχειρίζομαι.g: I lay my hands upon, slay, kill
διαχειρίζομαι.long: I lay my hands upon, and so: I slay, kill.
διαχειρίζομαι.sd: to handle thoroughly, i.e. lay violent hands upon
διαχειρίζομαι.der: from G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G5495 (χείρ);
διαχειρίζομαι.as:
* δια-χειρίζω
(< χείρ),
to have in hand, conduct, manage. Mid.
(a) = act.;
(b) in late writers (Polyb., FlJ, al.), to lay hands on, kill: c. acc, Ac 5:3026:21.†

διαπρίομαι.long: (lit: I saw through), I cut to the quick (with indignation and envy).
διαπρίομαι.sd: to saw asunder, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate
διαπρίομαι.der: from G1223 (διά) and the base of G4249 (πρίζω);
διαπρίομαι.as:
δια-πρίω
[in LXX: I Ch 20:3 (שׂוּר) * ;]
to saw asunder. Pass., metaph. (vernacular?), EV, cut to the heart: Ac 5:33; seq. τ. καρδίαις αὐτῶν, Ac 7:54.†

διαλύω.as:
δια-λύω
[in LXX for אבה, חבל, etc. ;]
to part asunder, dissolve; of an assembly, pass., to disperse: Ac 5:36.†

δουλόω.kj: bring into (be under) bondage, X given, become (make) servant
δουλόω.as:
δουλόω, -ῶ
(< δοῦλος), [in LXX for עבד ;]
to enslave, bring into bondage: Ac 7:6(LXX), II Pe 2:19; metaph., I Co 9:19; pass., seq. ἐν, ib. 7:15; τ. θεῷ, Ro 6:22; τ. δικαιοσύνῃ, Ro 6:18; οἴνῳ, Tit 2:3; ὑπὸ τὰ στοιχεῖα τ. κόσμου, Ga 4:3 (Cremer, 217).†

δικαστής.as:
δικαστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(< δικάζω), [in LXX for שֹׁפֵט ;]
a judge: Ac 7:27, 35(LXX).†
SYN.: κριτής, wh. "gives prominence to the mental process" (Thayer). δ. is the forensic term. In Attic law, the δικασταί were jurors, with a κριτής as presiding officer (LS, s.v.; Enc. Brit.11, xii, 504 f.).

διαδέχομαι.long: I receive in my turn, receive through another.
διαδέχομαι.sd: to receive in turn, i.e. (figuratively) succeed to
διαδέχομαι.as:
δια-δέχομαι
[in LXX for מִשְׁנֶה (Deiss., BS, 115), פַּרְבָּר ;]
to receive through another, receive in turn: Ac 7:45 (RV, in their turn; v. Field, Notes, 116).†

διαταγή.as:
† δια-ταγή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< διατάσσω), [in LXX: II Es 4:11 (פַּרְשֶׁגֶן)* ;]
in late writers (Deiss., LAE, 86 ff.) for cl. διάταξις (wh., however, is found in LXX, Ps 118 (119):91, al.);
(a)disposition (cf. διάταξις for צְבָא; Sm., IV Ki 23:4, Je 8:219:13); εἰς διαταγὰς ἀγγέλων, AV, by the disposition of angels (Alf., in l., Field, Notes, 116; but v. infr.): Ac 7:53;
(b)ordinance (C. I. 3465): Ro 13:2, Ac 7:53, R, txt. (and v. mg.; Page and EGT, in l.; but also v. supr.).†

διασπείρω.sd: to sow throughout, i.e. (figuratively) distribute in foreign lands
διασπείρω.as:
δια-σπείρω
[freq. in LXX for פּוּץ, etc. ;]
to scatter abroad, disperse: Ac 8:1, 411:19.†

Δαμασκός.as:
Δαμασκός, -οῦ, ἡ (Heb. דַּמֶּשֶׂק),
Damascus: Ac 9:2ff. 22:5ff. 26:12, 20, II Co 11:32, Ga 1:17.†

Δορκάς.long: Dorcas, the Greek name of Tabitha.
Δορκάς.as:
Δορκάς, -άδος, ἡ
(δορκάς, a gazelle),
Dorcas, also called Ταβειθά, q.v.: Ac 9:36, 39.†

διερωτάω.sd: to question throughout, i.e. ascertain by interrogation
διερωτάω.as:
* δι-ερωτάω, -ῶ
to find by inquiry: c. acc, Ac 10:17.†

διενθυμέομαι.as:
*† δι-ενθυμέομαι, -οῦμαι, depon.,
to consider, reflect: seq. περί, Ac 10:19.†

δημηγορέω.g: I make a public speech, address a multitude
δημηγορέω.long: I make a public speech, address a multitude.
δημηγορέω.sd: to be a people-gatherer, i.e. to address a public assembly
δημηγορέω.der: from a compound of G1218 (δῆμος) and G58 (ἀγορά);
δημηγορέω.as:
δημηγορέω, -ῶ
(< δῆμος, ἀγορεύω, to speak in the assembly), [in LXX: Pr 24:66 (30:31), IV Mac 5:15 * ;]
to deliver an oration: Ac 12:21.†

δῆμος.long: properly: the people, especially citizens of a Greek city in popular assembly, but in NT, multitude, rabble.
δῆμος.as:
δῆμος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for מִשְׁפָּחָה ;]
1.a district, country.
2.the common people, the people generally; esp. the people assembled: Ac 12:2217:519:30, 33.†
SYN.: λαός, the people at large: δ., the people as a body politic; opp. to δ. is ὄχλος, the unorganized multitude. ἔθνος, in sing., means in NT as in Gk. writers generally, a nation, but in pl. denotes the rest of mankind apart from the Jews: Gentiles. λ. also, rare in cl. (Att... λεώς), is freq. in LXX and NT, and usually limited to the chosen people, Israel (cf. Cl. Rev., i, 42 f.; Cremer, 689).

δρόμος.as:
δρόμος, -ου, ὁ
(< δραμεῖν, v.s. τρέχω) [in LXX chiefly for מְרוּצָה ;]
a course: fig., of life or ministry, Ac 13:2520:24, II Ti 4:7.†

Δέρβη.long: Derbe, a town in Lycaonia and in the southern part of the Roman province Galatia.
Δέρβη.sd: Derbe, a place in Asia Minor
Δέρβη.as:
Δέρβη, -ης, ἡ,
Derbe, a city of Lycaonia: Ac 14:6, 2016:1.†

δεσμοφύλαξ.g: a keeper of a prison, a jailer
δεσμοφύλαξ.long: a keeper of a prison, a jailer.
δεσμοφύλαξ.as:
*† δεσμο-φύλαξ, -κος, ὁ
(δεσμός, φύλαξ),
a prison-keeper, gaoler: Ac 16:23, 27, 36 (cf. ἀρχιδ-, Ge 39:21).†

δεισιδαίμων.g: respectful of what is divine, religious
δεισιδαίμων.long: respectful of what is divine; religious, perhaps, rather than superstitious (the usual meaning).
δεισιδαίμων.der: the compound of a derivative of the base of G1169 (δειλός) and G1142 (δαίμων);
δεισιδαίμων.as:
* δεισι-δαίμων, -ον
(< δείδω, to fear; δαίμων, deity)
reverent to the deity, religious; compar. -μονεστέρους (AV, too superstitious, R, txt., somewhat superstitious, a sense in wh. the word is sometimes used; cf. Field, Notes, 125), more religious, God fearing, than others, quite religious (Abbott, Essays, 105 ff.; Deiss., LAE, 285): Ac 17:22.†
SYN.: εὐσεβής (q.v.), θεοσεβής, θρῆσκος (Cremer, 681; DB, ext., 142 a).

Δάμαρις.sd: perhaps gentle; Damaris, an Athenian woman
Δάμαρις.der: probably from the base of G1150 (δαμάζω);
Δάμαρις.as:
Δάμαρις, -ιδος, ἡ
(< δάμαρ, poët., a wife),
Damaris: Ac 17:34.†

διακατελέγχομαι.der: middle voice from G1223 (διά) and a compound of G2596 (κατά) and G1651 (ἐλέγχω);

Δημήτριος.sd: Demetrius, the name of an Ephesian and of a Christian
Δημήτριος.as:
Δημήτριος, -ου, ὁ
Demetrius;
1. a silversmith, Ac 19:24, 38.
2. A Christian disciple, III Jo 12.†

διοπετής.der: from the alternate of G2203 (Ζεύς) and the alternate of G4098 (πίπτω);
διοπετής.as:
* διοπετής (written also διϊπ-), -ές
(< δῖος, πίπτω, v. Page on Ac, l.c.; DB, i, 605, n., ext., 112a; Field, Notes, 130 f.),
fallen from heaven (R, mg.): τὸ δ. (sc. ἄγαλμα, statue, image), Ac 19:35.†

Δερβαῖος.sd: a Derbæan or inhabitant of Derbe

διανύω.as:
** δι-ανύω
[in LXX: II Mac 12:17 * ;]
1.to accomplish fully, finish, complete: Ac 21:7 (EV).
2. In late writers (Xen., al., Clem., I ad Cor., xxv, 3), to continue: Ac, l.c. (Field, Notes, 134 f.).†

διαμάχομαι.as:
δια-μάχομαι
[in LXX for לחם ni., Da LXX 10:20; Si 8:1, 338:2851:19 * ;]
1.to struggle against.
2. In argument, to contend: Ac 23:9.†

διαγινώσκω.sd: to know thoroughly, i.e. ascertain exactly
διαγινώσκω.as:
δια-γινώσκω
(v. previous word), [in LXX chiefly for ידע, and cf. II Mac 9:15 ;]
1.to distinguish, ascertain exactly: Ac 23:15
2. As Athen. law-term, to determine: τὰ καθ’ ὑμᾶς, your case, Ac 24:22 (Cremer, 673).†

δεξιολάβος.g: one posted on the right hand, a spear-man
δεξιολάβος.long: one posted on the right hand, a spear-man.
δεξιολάβος.sd: a guardsman (as if taking the right) or light-armed soldier
δεξιολάβος.as:
* δεξιολάβος, -ου, ὁ
(< δεξιός, λαμβάνω),
a kind of soldier, prob. a spearman (Vg., lancearius) or slinger: Ac 23:23.†

διακούω.g: I hear throughout, of a judicial hearing
διακούω.long: I hear throughout, of a judicial hearing.
διακούω.sd: to hear throughout, i.e. patiently listen (to a prisoner's plea)
διακούω.der: middle voice from G1223 (διά) and G191 (ἀκούω);
διακούω.as:
δι-ακούω
[in LXX: De 1:16 (שׁמע), Jb 9:33 (יָדשִׁית hi.)* ;]
to hear through, hear fully; technically, to hear judicially (as De, l.c.; of. Deiss., BS, 230): Ac 23:35.†

διόρθωμα.der: from a compound of G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G3717 (ὀρθός), meaning to straighten thoroughly;
διόρθωμα.as:
* διόρθωμα, -τος, τό
(< διορθόω, to make straight, set right),
a correction, reform: Ac 24:3.†

Δρούσιλλα.long: Drusilla (born A.D. 39), daughter of Herod Agrippa I.
Δρούσιλλα.sd: Drusilla, a member of the Herodian family
Δρούσιλλα.der: a feminine diminutive of Drusus (a Roman name);
Δρούσιλλα.as:
Δρούσιλλα (Rec. Δρουσίλλα), ης, ἡ,
Drusilla, wife of Felix: Ac 24:24.†

διετία.long: a period of two years, two years; according to ancient practice this means any period between one and two years.
διετία.as:
† διετία, -ας, ἡ
(< διετής), [in LXX (Græc. Ven.): Ge 41:145:5 * ;]
the space of two years: Ac 24:2728:30.†

διάδοχος.as:
διά-δοχος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ
(< διαδέχομαι), [in LXX: I Ch 18:17 (לְיַד), II Ch 26:11 (שַׂר) 28:7 (מִשְׁנֶה), Si 46:148:8, II Mac 4:2914:26 * ;]
a successor: Ac 24:27 (for usage in LXX and π. in sense of court official, v. Deiss., BS, 115).†

δεισιδαιμονία.long: religion in general; in a bad sense: superstition.
δεισιδαιμονία.as:
*† δεισιδαιμονία, -ας, ἡ
(< δεισιδαίμων, q.v.);
1.fear of the gods;
(a)piety, religion;
(b)superstition.
2. Objectively, a religion: Ac 25:19 (Cremer, 72, 682).†

διάγνωσις.long: judicial examination, decision; an act of discernment.
διάγνωσις.as:
** διά-γνωσις, -εως, ἡ
(< διαγιγνώσκω), [in LXX: Wi 3:18 * ;]
1.a distinguishing, also as medical term.
2. As law-term (Lat. cognitio), determination, decision: Ac 25:21 (Cremer, 674).†

δωδεκάφυλον.as:
*† δωδεκά-φυλος, -ον
(< δώδεκα, φυλή),
of twelve tribes: as subst. neut., τό δ. (cf. λαὸςὁ δ., Sibyll. Orac.), the twelve tribes, Ac 26:7.†

δεσμώτης.as:
δεσμώτης, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX for אסר, מַסְגֵּר ;]
a prisoner: Ac 27:1, 42.†

διατελέω.sd: to accomplish thoroughly, i.e. (subjectively) to persist
διατελέω.as:
δια-τελέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: De 9:7 (היה), Je 20:7, 18 (כּלה), Es 8:13, II Mac 5:27 * ;]
prop. trans., to accomplish; used with ellipse of obj. as intrans. (Bl., § 81, 1), and joined to participles (in Ac, l.c., to adj.; v. Bl., § 73, 4) with adverbial sense (= continuously), to continue: Ac 27:33.†

διθάλασσος.long: between two seas, which has sea on both sides.
διθάλασσος.sd: having two seas, i.e. a sound with a double outlet
διθάλασσος.as:
*† διθάλασσος, -ον
(δις, θύλασσα);
1.divided into two seas (as the Euxine, Strab., ii, 522).
2.dividing the sea: τόπον δ., a tongue of land, or reef, running out into the sea: Ac 27:41.†

διαφεύγω.as:
δια-φεύγω
[in LXX: Jos 8:22 (פָּלִיט), ib. 10:28 (שָׂרִיד), etc. ;]
to flee through, escape: Ac 27:42.†

δίκη.long: (a) (originally: custom, usage) right, justice, (b) process of law, judicial hearing, (c) execution of sentence, punishment, penalty, (d) justice, vengeance.
δίκη.sd: right (as self-evident), i.e. justice (the principle, a decision, or its execution)
δίκη.as:
δίκη, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX for נקם, ריב, etc. ;]
1.custom.
2.right.
3.a judicial hearing; hence its result, the execution of a sentence, punishment: δ. τίνειν, II Th 1:9; δ. υπεχειν, Ju 7.
4. Personified (cf. Lat. Justitia), justice, vengeance: Ac 28:4.†

δυσεντέριον.as:
*† δυσεντέριον, -ου, τό
(ἔντερον, intestine), late form of δυσεντερία (Rec., l.c.),
dysentery: Ac 28:8.†

Διόσκουροι.long: the Dioscuri, Castor and Pollux, sons of Zeus and Leda, and patrons of sailors.
Διόσκουροι.sd: sons of Jupiter, i.e. the twins Dioscuri
Διόσκουροι.der: from the alternate of G2203 (Ζεύς) and a form of the base of G2877 (κοράσιον);
Διόσκουροι.as:
Διόσ-κουροι, -ων, οἱ
(Ion. and κοινή form of Att., Διόσκοροι; < Διός, gen. of Ζεύς + κόρος, a son),
the Dioscuri (Castor and Pollux), twin sons of Zeus and Leda (RV, The Twin Brothers): Ac 28:11.†

δευτεραῖος.g: on the second day, on the next day
δευτεραῖος.long: adj. where English requires an adv., on the second day, on the next day.
δευτεραῖος.sd: secondary, i.e. (specially) on the second day
δευτεραῖος.as:
* δευτεραῖος, -α, -ον
(< δεύτερος),
adj. with adverbial sense;
on the second day: δευτεραῖοι ἤλθομεν, Ac 28:13.†

δικαιοκρισία.as:
† δικαιοκρισία, -ας, ἡ
righteous judgment: Ro 2:5 (cf. τ. δικαίας κρίσεως, II Th 1:5; τὴν δ. κ., Jo 7:24. For use in π., v. Deiss., LAE, 89 f.).†

δολιόω.long: I act deceitfully, deceive, use fraud.
δολιόω.as:
† δολιόω
(< δόλιος), [in LXX: Nu 25:18, Ps 104 (105):25 (נָכַל), Ps 5:6 (חָלַק hi.) * ;]
to deceive: ἐδολιοῦσαν (-σαν, freq. in κοινή Gk. for impf. 3rd pers. pl.), Ro 3:13(LXX).†

διαστολή.as:
δια-στολή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< διαστέλλω), [in LXX for פְּדוּת: Ex 8:23(19), etc. ;]
1.a separation.
2.a distinction, difference: Ro 3:2210:12, I Co 14:7.†

δικαίωσις.long: acquittal, justifying, justification, a process of absolution.
δικαίωσις.as:
δικαίωσις, -εως, ἡ
(< δικαιόω), [in LXX for מִשְׁפָּט, Le 24:22 * ;]
the act of pronouncing righteous, justification, acquittal: Ro 4:255:18 (Cremer, 199).†

δοκιμή.g: a trial, proof; tried, approved character
δοκιμή.long: a trial, proof; tried, approved character.
δοκιμή.sd: test (abstractly or concretely); by implication, trustiness
δοκιμή.as:
*† δοκιμή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< δόκιμος), [in Sm.: Ps 67 (68):31 * ;]
1. the process of trial, proving, test: II Co 8:29:13.
2. The result of trial, approval, approvedness, proof : Ro 5:4, II Co 2:913:3, Phl 2:22 (Cremer, 212, 701).†

δώρημα.as:
** δώρημα, -τος, τό
(< δωρέω), [in LXX: Si 31 (34):18* ;]
a gift, boon: Ro 5:16, Ja 1:17.†
SYN.: v.s. δόμα.

δουλεία.as:
δουλεία (T, -λία), -ας, ἡ
(< δουλεύω), [in LXX, as Ex 13:3, for עֶבֶד and cognates ;]
slavery, bondage: Ro 8:15, 21, Ga 4:245:1, He 2:15.†

διάφορος.as:
διά-φορος, -ον
(< διαφέρω), [in LXX for שְׁנָא (Da 7:7, 19); also as in Polyb., iv, 188, al., Τὸ δ., τὰ δ., money: Si 27:142:5, II Mac 3:6 ;]
1.different: Ro 12:6, He 9:10.
2.excellent: compar., -ώτερος, He 1:48:6.†

διάκρισις.long: distinguishing; hence: deciding, passing sentence on; the act of judgment, discernment.
διάκρισις.as:
διά-κρισις, -εως, ἡ
(< διακρίνω) [in LXX for מִפְלָשׂ, Jb 37:16 * ;]
the act of judgment, discernment: Ro 14:1, I Co 12:10, He 5:14.†

δυνατέω.long: I am powerful, have power, am able, am mighty.
δυνατέω.as:
δυνατέω, -ῶ
(< δυνατός),
to be able, be powerful, mighty: c. inf., Ro 14:4, II Co 9:8; absol., opp. to ἀσθενῶII Co 13:3.†

δόκιμος.sd: properly, acceptable (current after assayal), i.e. approved
δόκιμος.as:
δόκιμος, -ον
(< δέκομαι = δέχομαι) [in LXX for זקק pu., etc. ;]
primarily of metals, tested, accepted, approved: of persons, Ro 14:1816:10, I Co 11:19, II Co 10:1813:7, II Ti 2:15, Ja 1:12 (Cremer, 212, 697).†

διχοστασία.der: from a derivative of G1364 (δίς) and G4714 (στάσις);
διχοστασία.as:
** διχοστασία, -ας, ἡ
(< διχοστατέω, to stand apart), [in LXX: I Mac 3:29 * ;]
standing apart, dissension: Ro 16:17, Ga 5:20.†

δηλόω.as:
δηλόω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for ידע ;]
to make plain, declare: c. acc., I Co 3:13, Col 1:8, He 9:812:27; c. dat. pers., II Pe 1:14; c. dat. pers., seq. περί (pass.), I Co 1:11; seq. εἰς, I Pe 1:11.†
SYN.: ἐμφανίζω, to make manifest, render visible to the sight; δ. to render evident to the mind.

δράσσομαι.long: I take hold of, grasp, catch.
δράσσομαι.der: perhaps akin to the base of G1404 (δράκων) (through the idea of capturing);
δράσσομαι.as:
δράσσομαι
[in LXX for נשׁק pi., Ps 2:12; elsewhere קמץ, as Le 2:2 ;]
to grasp with the hand, to lay hold of : metaph., c. acc (M, Pr., 65), I Co 3:19(LXX).†

δυσφημέω.long: evil report, defamation, words of ill omen.
δυσφημέω.der: from a compound of G1418 (δυσ-) and G5345 (φήμη);
δυσφημέω.as:
** δυσφημέω, -ώ
(< δύσφημος, slanderous), [in LXX: I Mac 7:41 * ;]
1. intrans., to use evil words (Æsch.).
2. Trans., to speak ill of, defame (Soph.): pass., I Co 4:13.†

διόπερ.as:
** διό-περ conjunct. (διό, q.v., strengthened by πέρ),
[in LXX: Jth 8:17; II Mac 5 * ;]
for which very reason: I Co 8:1310:14.†

δουλαγωγέω.long: I bring into subjection, enslave, treat as a slave.
δουλαγωγέω.sd: to be a slave-driver, i.e. to enslave (figuratively, subdue)
δουλαγωγέω.der: from a presumed compound of G1401 (δοῦλος) and G71 (ἄγω);
δουλαγωγέω.as:
*† δουλαγωγέω, -ῶ
(< δοῦλος, ἄγω),
to make a slave, bring into bondage: I Co 9:27 (Cremer, 703).†

διαίρεσις.as:
δι-αίρεσις, -εως, ἡ
(< διαιρέω), [in LXX chiefly for מַחֲלֹקֶת ;]
1.a distinction, diference.
2.a division, distribution: I Co 12:4-6 (cf. διαιρέω; Cremer, 616).†

διερμηνευτής.as:
*† δι-ερμηνευτής, -οῦ, ὁ
(< διερμηνεύω),
an interpreter: I Co 14:28.†

δολόω.as:
δολόω, -ῶ
(δόλος) [in LXX: Ps 14 (15):3 (רגל), Ps 35 (36):2 (חלק hi.) * ;]
1.to ensnare.
2. As of wine, to adulterate, corrupt: τ. λόγον τ. θεοῦ, II Co 4:2.†
SYN.: καπηλεύω q.v.

δυσφημία.long: evil report, defamation, words of ill omen.
δυσφημία.der: from a compound of G1418 (δυσ-) and G5345 (φήμη);
δυσφημία.as:
** δυσφημία, -ας, ἡ
(< δύσφημος, slanderous), [in LXX: I Mac 7:38, III Mac 2:20 * ;]
evil-speaking, defamation: opp. to εὐφημία, II Co 6:8.†

δότης.as:
† δότης, -ου, ὁ
(< δίδωμι), [in LXX: Pr 22:8 * ;]
= δοτήρ,
a giver: II Co 9:7(LXX) (not elsewhere).†

δόλιος.as:
δόλιος, -α, -ον
(< δόλος), [in LXX—chiefly in Pss, Pr, Si—forמִרִמָהetc.;]
deceitful: II Co 11:13.†

δίψος.as:
δίψος, -εος (-ους), τό
(late form of δίψα), [in LXX chiefly for צָמֵא and cognates ;]
thirst: II Co 11:27.†

Δαμασκηνός.long: a Damascene, an inhabitant of Damascus.
Δαμασκηνός.sd: a Damascene or inhabitant of Damascus

δάκνω.long: I bite; hence: I backbite, harm seriously.
δάκνω.der: a prolonged form of a primary root;
δάκνω.as:
δάκνω
[in LXX for נשׁךְ, Ge 49:17, al., exc. De 8:15 (שׂרף) ;]
to bite: metaph., Ga 5:15.†

δόσις.sd: a giving; by implication, (concretely) a gift
δόσις.as:
δόσις, -εως, ἡ
(δίδωμι) [in LXX for חֹק (Ge 47:22), מַתָּך, מַתַּת (Pr 21:1425:14), freq. in Si. ;]
1. properly, the act of giving: Phl 4:15.
2. Objectively, a gift: Ja 1:17.†
SYN.: v.s. δόμα

δυναμόω.long: I empower, fill with power, strengthen.
δυναμόω.as:
† δυναμόω, -ῶ
(< δύναμις), [in LXX for עזז, Ps 51 (52):767 (68):28; גּבר pi., hi., Ec 10:10, Da TH 9:27 * ;]
to make strong, strengthen: Eph 6:10 (WH, mg.; ἐνδυν-, WH, txt., RV), Col 1:11, He 11:34.†

δογματίζομαι.long: I subject to regulations, decree; mid: I subject myself to regulations, am decree-ridden.
δογματίζομαι.sd: to prescribe by statute, i.e. (reflexively) to submit to, ceremonially rule
δογματίζομαι.as:
† δογματίζω
[in LXX: Es 3:9 (כָּתַב ni.), Da LXX 2:13, 15 (דָּתָא, דָּת), I Es 6:34, II Mac 10:315:36, III Mac 4:11 * ;]
to decree. Mid., to subject oneself to an ordinance: Col 2:20.†

Δημᾶς.long: Demas, a helper of Paul in Rome.
Δημᾶς.as:
Δημᾶς, ὁ
(perh. contracted from Δημήτριος),
Demas, a companion of St. Paul: Col 4:14, Phm 24, II Ti 4:10.†

διαβεβαιόομαι.sd: to confirm thoroughly (by words), i.e. asseverate
διαβεβαιόομαι.der: middle voice of a compound of G1223 (διά) and G950 (βεβαιόω);
διαβεβαιόομαι.as:
* δια-βεβαιόομαι, -οῦμαι
to affirm confidently: Tit 3:8; seq. περί, I Ti 1:7 (Cremer, 140).†

διώκτης.as:
*† διώκτης, -ου, ὁ
(< διώκω),
a persecutor: I Ti 1:13.†

διάγω.g: I spend time, pass time, live
διάγω.long: (either trans. or intrans.), I spend time, pass time, live.
διάγω.as:
δι-άγω
[in LXX for עבר hi., etc. ;]
1.to carry over.
2. Of time, to pass: βίον, I Ti 2:2; absol., to live, seq. ἐν, Tit 3:3.†

διδακτικός.g: able to teach, apt to teach
διδακτικός.long: able to teach, apt to teach.
διδακτικός.as:
διδακτικός, -ή, -όν
(= cl. διδασκαλικός)
apt at teaching: I Ti 3:2, II Ti 2:24.†

δίλογος.sd: equivocal, i.e. telling a different story
δίλογος.as:
*† δίλογος, -ον
(< δίς, λέγω),
1. in sense of διλογεῖν, -ία (Xen.), given to repetition.
2. In NT, prob. (cf. δίγλωσσος, Pr 11:13, Si 5:9) double-tongued: I Ti 3:8.†

διαπαρατριβή.as:
δια-παρα-τριβή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< παρατριβή, friction, irritation)
mutual irritation (Field, Notes, 211), wrangling: I Ti 6:5 (Rec. παραδιατριβή).†

διατροφή.der: from a compound of G1223 (διά) and G5142 (τρέφω);
διατροφή.as:
** δια-τροφή, ῆς, ἡ
(< διατρέφω, to support, sustain), [in LXX: I Mac 6:49 * ;]
food, nourishment: I Ti 6:8.†

δειλία.as:
δειλία, -ας, ἡ
(< δειλός), [in LXX for אֵימָה, מְחִתָּה, etc. ;]
cowardice, timidity (never in good sense): II Ti 1:7.†
SYN.: φόβος, fear, in general, good or bad; εὐλάβεια (q.v.), apprehension generally, but chiefly pious fear, "that careful and watchful reverence which pays regard to every circumstance in that with which it has to deal" (cf. Tr., Syn., § x).†

Δαλματία.long: Dalmatia, a province of the Roman Empire, east of the Adriatic, a later name for part of what was earlier called Illyricum.
Δαλματία.as:
Δαλματία (L, Δελ-), -ας, ἡ
Dalmatia, a part of Illyria on E. coast of the Adriatic: II Ti 4:10.†

δήπου.long: of course, indeed, qualifying and yet strengthening the assertion.
δήπου.sd: a particle of asseveration; indeed doubtless
δήπου.as:
* δή-που (WH, δή που),
indef. adv.,
mostly in sense of surely, of course, we know: He 2:16 T (WH, δή που).†

δοκιμασία.as:
** δοκιμασία, -ας, ἡ
(< δοκιμάζω), [in LXX: Si 6:21 * ;]
a testing, proving: He 3:9(LXX).†

δίστομος.long: (lit: twain-mouthed; hence: of a sword, as a drinker of blood), two-edged.
δίστομος.as:
δίστομος, -ον
(< δίς, στόμα), [in LXX: Jg 3:16, Ps 149:6, Pr 5:4 (פִּּיּוֹת), Si 21:3 * ;]
1. of rivers and roads, double-mouthed, double branching.
2. Of swords (Eur.; LXX, ll. c.), two-edged: He 4:12, Re 1:162:12.†

διϊκνέομαι.long: I pass through (to), come through (to), pierce.
διϊκνέομαι.der: from G1223 (διά) and the base of G2425 (ἱκανός);
διϊκνέομαι.as:
δι-ικνέομαι (Rec. διϊκ-), -οῦμαι,
[in LXX for בּרח hi., Ex 26:28 * ;]
to go through, penetrate: He 4:12.†

δυσερμήνευτος.long: difficult to interpret, hard to be understood.
δυσερμήνευτος.der: from G1418 (δυσ-) and a presumed derivative of G2059 (ἑρμηνεύω);

δεκάτη.sd: a tenth, i.e. as a percentage or (technically) tithe
δεκάτη.as:
δεκάτη, -ης, ἡ prop. fem. (sc. μέρος) of δέκατος, -η, -ον,
[in LXX for מַעֲשֵׂר: Ge 14:20, Ne 12:44, et al. ;]
a tenth part, a tithe: He 7:2, 4, 8, 9 (for a curious inversion of the Biblical use, v. MM, s.v.).†

διηνεκής.sd: carried through, i.e. (adverbially with G1519 (εἰς) and G3588 (ὁ) prefixed) perpetually
διηνεκής.der: neuter of a compound of G1223 (διά) and a derivative of an alternate of G5342 (φέρω);
διηνεκής.as:
** δι-ηνεκής, -ές
(< διήνεγκα, aor. of διαφέρω) [in Sm.: Ps 47 (48):15, 88 (89):30 ;]
unbroken, continuous: adverbially, εἰς τὸ δ., continually (for exx., v. Deiss., BS, 251), He 7:310:1, 12, 14.†

δεκατόω.sd: to tithe, i.e. to give or take a tenth
δεκατόω.as:
† δεκατόω, -ῶ,
= cl. -τεύω (< δεκάτη), [in LXX: Ne 10:37 (38) (עשׂר pi.) * ;]
to take tithe of: c. acc. pers., He 7:6; pass. to pay tithe: He 7:9.†

διόρθωσις.der: from a compound of G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G3717 (ὀρθός), meaning to straighten thoroughly;
διόρθωσις.as:
* διόρθωσις, -εως, ἡ (v. supr.),
1.a making straight.
2.a reforming, reformation (used in late writers of laws, etc.): He 9:10 (Cremer, 807).†

δάμαλις.der: probably from the base of G1150 (δαμάζω);
δάμαλις.as:
δάμαλις, -εως, ἡ
(fem. of δαμάλης, a bullock), [in LXX chiefly for פָּרָה, עֶגְלָה ;]
a heifer, He 9:13.†

δημιουργός.long: an artisan, builder, maker; one who labors for the public.
δημιουργός.sd: a worker for the people, i.e. mechanic (spoken of the Creator)
δημιουργός.as:
** δημιουργός, -οῦ, ὑ
(< δῆμος, ἔργον), [in LXX: II Mac 4:1 * ;]
1.one who works for the people.
2. Univ., an author, builder, maker; the maker of the world (Xen., Mem., I, 4, 9, al.), He 11:10.†
SYN.: κτίστης, creator, τεχνίτης, craftsman, designer. In He, l.c., τ. has reference to the plan, δ. to its execution.

διάταγμα.as:
† διά-ταγμα, -τος, τό
(< διατάσσω), [in LXX: II Es 7:11 (נִשְׁתְּוָן), Es 3:13, Wi 11:7 * ;]
an edict, mandate: He 11:23.†

δέρμα.long: the skin or hide of an animal.
δέρμα.as:
δέρμα, -τος, τό
(< δέρω), [in LXX for עוֹר ;]
the skin, hide of beasts: ἐν αἰγίοις δ., He 11:37.†

δέος.as:
** δέος, -ους, τό
(< δείδω), [in LXX: II Mac 3:17, 3012:2213:1615:23 * ;]
fear, awe, reverence: μετὰ εὐλαβείας καὶ δ., He 12:28.†
SYN.: δειλία, φόβος.

δοκίμιον.g: a test, trial, what is genuine
δοκίμιον.long: a test, trial, what is genuine.
δοκίμιον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of G1382 (δοκιμή);
δοκίμιον.as:
δοκίμιον, -ου, τό
[in LXX: Pr 17:327:21 (מַצְרֵף) * ;]
usually regarded as a variant form of δοκιμεῖον, a test, and so perh. Ja 1:3 (v. Mayor, in l.), but see next word (cf. Cremer, 212, 702).†

δίψυχος.long: (lit: of two souls, of two selves), double-minded, wavering.
δίψυχος.sd: two-spirited, i.e. vacillating (in opinion or purpose)
δίψυχος.as:
*† δίψυχος, -ον
(< δίς, ψυχή),
of two minds, wavering: Ja 1:84:8 (Cremer, 588; DB, iv, 528).†

δελεάζω.g: I allure, entice by a bait
δελεάζω.as:
* δελεάζω
(< δέλεαρ, a bait),
to allure by a bait: metaph., to allure, entice: c. acc, II Pe 2:14, 18; pass., Ja 1:14.†

δαιμονιώδης.as:
**† δαιμονιώδης, -ες
(< δαιμόνιον, εἶδος), [in Sm.: Ps 90(91):6 * ;]
demon-like: Ja 3:15 (Cremer, 171).†

διαυγάζω.long: I shine through, dawn (of the light coming through the shadows).
διαυγάζω.sd: to glimmer through, i.e. break (as day)
διαυγάζω.as:
**† δι-αυγάζω
[in Aq.: Jb 25:5 * ;]
to shine through, to dawn: II Pe 1:19 (cf. ἕως οὗ διαπνεύσῃ ἡ ἡμέρα, Ca 2:17).†

δυσνόητος.der: from G1418 (δυσ-) and a derivative of G3539 (νοιέω);
δυσνόητος.as:
* δυσνόητος, -ον
(< νοέω),
hard to understand: II Pe 3:16.†

Διοτρέφης.sd: Jove-nourished; Diotrephes, an opponent of Christianity
Διοτρέφης.der: from the alternate of G2203 (Ζεύς) and G5142 (τρέφω);
Διοτρέφης.as:
Διοτρέφης (Rec. -τρεψής), -ες
(< Διός, gen. of Ζεύς + τρέφω: cherished by Zeus),
as proper name, Diotrephes: III Jo 9.†

δεῖγμα.long: an example, type; a thing shown.
δεῖγμα.as:
* δεῖγμα, -τος, τό
(< δείκνυμι);
1. (cl.) a thing shown, a specimen.
2. = cl. παράδ- (cf. ὑπόδ-, II Pe 2:6), an example (a warning): Ju 7.†

δισμυριάς.as:
**† δισ-μυριάς, -άδος, ἡ,
[in LXX: II Mac 6 * ;]
twice ten thousand: Re 9:16 (LT; δὶς μυριάδες, WH; δύο μ., Rec.).†

δράκων.long: a dragon or huge serpent; met: Satan.
δράκων.sd: a fabulous kind of serpent (perhaps as supposed to fascinate)
δράκων.der: probably from an alternate form of (to look);
δράκων.as:
δράκων, -οντος, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for תַּנִּין ;]
a dragon, a mythical monster: fig., of Satan, Re 12:3-1713:2, 4, 1116:1320:2.†

διάδημα.der: from a compound of G1223 (διά) and G1210 (δέω);
διάδημα.as:
διάδημα, -τος, τό
(< διαδέω, to bind round), [in LXX for כֶּתֶר (as Es 1:11), etc. ;]
the band round the τιάρα of a Persian king; a diadem, the badge of royalty: Re 12:313:119:12.†
SYN.: στέφανος, the badge of "victory, of valour, of nuptial joy, of festal gladness " (but v. M, Th., i, 219; cf. DB, i, 530, 604).

Διάβολος.long: (adj. used often as a noun), slanderous; with the article: the Slanderer (par excellence), the Devil.
Διάβολος.as:
διάβολος, -ον
(< διαβάλλω, q.v.) [in LXX for שָׂטָן (as Jb 1:6), exc. Es 7:48:1 (צַר, צָרַר) ;]
slanderous, accusing falsely. As subst., ὁ, ἡ, δ.;
(a) generally (of. Es, ll. c.), a slanderer, false accuser: I Ti 3:6, 7 (CGT, in l., but v. infr.) 3:11, II Ti 3:3, Tit 2:3;
(b) as chiefly in LXX, of Satan, the Accuser, the Devil: Mt 4:1, 5, 8, 1113:3925:41, Lk 4:2, 3, 6, 138:12, Jo 13:2, Ac 10:38, Eph 4:276:11, I Ti 3:6, 7 (but v. supr.), II Ti 2:26, He 2:14, Ja 4:7, I Pe 5:8, Ju 9, Re 2:1012:9, 1220:2, 10; εἶναι ἐκ τοῦ δ., Jo 8:44, I Jo 3:8; τέκνα τοῦ δ., I Jo 3:10; υἱὸς, Ac 13:10; metaph., of Judas, Jo 6:70 (Cremer, 121; DCG, ii, 605).†

διπλόω.as:
* διπλόω, -ῶ
(< διπλόος),
to double: δ. τὰ διπλᾶ, Re 18:6.†

διαυγής.as:
** διαυγής, -ές
(< αὐγή), [in Aq.: Pr 16:2 * ;]
transparent: Re 21:21.†
